JobCreate.description:

else the settings default; the server stores it in ``options.provider``. ``local`` jobs need an
upload and downloaded models (422 otherwise); the resolved ASR model and device are pinned in
``options.local``. ``file_url`` jobs are cloud-only (D3). ``options.terms`` is rebuilt
server-side from ``term_set_ids`` + ``extra_terms``.

patch.description:
Apply ops in order to ``segments`` / ``speakers`` / ``corrections``; ``original`` is
immutable (rule 9). All ops are validated before anything is written (all-or-nothing).
With ``expected_updated_at`` the patch is refused (409) if the transcript changed since.

(front matter, summary if any, speaker table, transcript; docs/research/siyuan-export.md).

post.description:
[5b] L3: ask the DashScope LLM for corrections of mis-heard words. Opt-in, costs money
and sends the segment text to the cloud; results are ``suggested`` corrections for review,
never applied automatically.

``segments <- original``. Speaker names/colours are kept; any speaker id used by the
original but missing from the list is added back.

Create a SiYuan document from the current segments (SiYuan-flavoured Markdown: summary,
speaker table, one block per turn with ``custom-asr-speaker`` / ``-start`` / ``-end``
attributes) and set ``custom-asr-*`` document attributes and tags. Every call creates a new
document; an existing path gets a `` (2)`` suffix.

422.description: SiYuan not configured, no notebook, or an invalid path.

502.description: SiYuan unreachable or refused the request.

put.description:
Rename / recolour speakers; an id not in the transcript yet adds a new speaker (for a
voice diarization missed). Speakers not listed are unchanged. With ``expected_updated_at``
the update is refused (409) if the transcript changed since.

404.description: Transcript not found, or no summary yet.

post.description:
M11: summarise the current segments with the DashScope LLM (overview, key points,
decisions, action items) and store the result, replacing an earlier one. Opt-in: it costs
money and sends the transcript text and speaker names to the cloud.

Single-request multipart upload (curl; the UI uses chunked upload, D11).

Form fields: ``file`` (the audio/video file) and ``target_dir`` (absolute, or relative to the
first upload root).
Start a chunked upload: ``total_parts`` parts of ``part_size`` bytes (last one shorter).
Register a file that already exists inside an upload root (no transfer).

Assemble the parts in order into ``target_dir`` and probe the result.

Idempotent for an hour: repeating ``complete`` for a session that already completed returns
the same upload with 200 (a concurrent repeat waits for the first call).

put.description:
Raw part body (``application/octet-stream``); read via ``request.stream()``.

Every part must be exactly ``part_size`` bytes except the last. Re-sending a part replaces
it (idempotent).
